purpose: Treat finite slab depth as an explicit parent-model uncertainty and robustness axis. Determine whether SI-relevant parent observables and carrier structures are stable across independently admitted finite-slab approximations without converting a failed absolute clean-surface convergence gate into a pass.

source_context.source_rule: These values establish the finite-slab uncertainty problem only. They do not calibrate an SI promotion threshold.

parent_ensemble.semantics: two independently characterized finite approximations to one physical parent substrate
parent_ensemble.winner_selection_forbidden: Do not choose L15 or L17 because one gives a more favorable child correspondence or inheritance result.
parent_ensemble.matched_comparison_requirement: Any thickness-robustness observable used for SI must be evaluated under computationally matched conditions sufficient to isolate slab-depth dependence. If the original source calculations co-vary vacuum, reciprocal sampling, supercell, or other numerical settings, recompute the compared observable under a matched protocol or report the thickness effect as confounded/nonidentifiable.

scalar.absolute_surface_excess: Retain the Chemistry absolute convergence HOLD and its numerical discrepancy in U_scalar. A scalar HOLD does not automatically erase separately demonstrated modal or conglomeration robustness.
scalar.other_scalars: Report finite-thickness spread continuously with provenance. No scalar may borrow a pass threshold from another view.

modal.required_geometry: Compare only prospectively defined shared physical degrees of freedom, preferably nested near-surface depth projections, with common mass normalization.
primary_objects: shared-region mass-weighted Hessian or dynamical operator
modal.degeneracy_rule: Use invariant subspaces/projectors for thickness-induced splitting, merging, crowding, or basis rotation rather than forcing one-to-one eigenvector identity.

primary_objects: projected surface resolvent or Green function
substrate self-energy or embedding contribution when independently derived
parent-to-adsorbate coupling block once the child protocol is independently frozen
conglomeration.rule: A downstream relative-energy or coupling observable may be adequate even while an unrelated absolute surface scalar remains unconverged, but the scope of that adequacy must be stated exactly.

perspective_rules.relationship_R: Report whether scalar, modal, and conglomeration thickness responses agree or disagree. Do not collapse them to one master slab score.
perspective_rules.uncertainty_U: Finite-thickness disagreement is propagated as an explicit uncertainty/refusal contribution. Precision in one view cannot erase thickness sensitivity in another required view.

candidate_continuous_diagnostics.projected_operator_change: delta_D = ||P D_17 P^T - P D_15 P^T|| / ||P D_17 P^T||, with norm, P, coordinate map, and mass metric frozen before child carrier inspection.
candidate_continuous_diagnostics.subspace_change: Compare Pi_15 and Pi_17 using principal angles/projector norms over a parent-only, prospectively defined carrier set or frequency window.
candidate_continuous_diagnostics.projected_resolvent_change: Compare G_15(omega)=P[(omega+i eta)^2 M-D_15]^{-1}P^T and G_17(omega) under a parent-only frozen omega window and eta convention.
candidate_continuous_diagnostics.depth_profile: Repeat shared-region diagnostics over a nested family of prospectively declared surface-depth projections to determine whether the relevant parent structure is localized or remains thickness-sensitive.
candidate_continuous_diagnostics.threshold_policy: Report these continuously with numerical uncertainty. This candidate protocol introduces no physical support/pass threshold.

child_prediction_rule.when_available: After the CO/Cu child governing object and parent-child mapping are independently frozen, generate the same prospective child prediction from each admissible parent-ensemble member.
child_prediction_rule.robust_pattern: If L15- and L17-based predictions agree within propagated thickness/numerical uncertainty and the independently computed child is compatible with both while modal-scramble, coupling-rewire, and zero-coupling controls lose the correspondence, report thickness-robust supporting evidence without changing v0.2 promotion semantics.
child_prediction_rule.sensitive_pattern: If the inheritance-relevant correspondence, prediction, or evidence classification materially depends on choosing L15 versus L17, report THICKNESS_SENSITIVE or UNRESOLVED rather than selecting the favorable thickness.
child_prediction_rule.prediction_interval_semantics: An ensemble envelope is a finite-parent-model uncertainty region, not a probability distribution unless an independent statistical model licenses that interpretation.

finite_size_correction_rule.reason: Metal slabs can exhibit quantum-size oscillations and absolute surface-energy drift can reflect slab/bulk-reference inconsistency. A monotone decay law must not be inferred from L15 and L17 alone.
finite_size_correction_rule.promotion_requirement: Any finite-size correction or extrapolation model selected after L17 is known must be validated on a prospectively withheld future rung or an independent external system before it is used to promote a physical convergence claim.

current_scope: software/method architecture only until provenance-complete matched L15/L17 SI-relevant parent objects exist
